items.followUp: Which protocol is commonly used to send e-mail?

rubric.why: Identifies the protocol used to send e-mail.

rubric.description: States that SMTP is used to send e-mail.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for its correct function.

modelAnswer: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send e-mail.
POP3 or IMAP may be used to receive e-mail.

items.followUp: What is meant by a communication channel in data communication?

rubric.why: Identifies the exchange of data as central to data communication.
rubric.description: States that data is exchanged or transferred.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning data transfer or exchange.

rubric.description: States that data is exchanged between devices, or from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the endpoints.

modelAnswer: Data communication is the exchange of data between two or more devices.
The devices communicate through a transmission medium.

items.followUp: What is the role of a web browser when a user opens a web page?

rubric.why: Shows that the server responds to a request from a client.
rubric.description: States that a web server receives a request from a client or browser.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the request.

rubric.why: Identifies what the server returns to the client.
rubric.description: States that the server sends the requested web page or data back.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the response.

modelAnswer: A web server receives a request for a web page from a client, such as a browser.
It processes the request and sends the requested page or data back to the client, usually using HTTP or HTTPS.

rubric.why: Describes the client's role in requesting resources.
rubric.description: States that a client requests a service or resource.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the request role.

rubric.why: Identifies the server with which the client communicates.
rubric.description: States that the client communicates with or receives services from a server.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the server relationship.

modelAnswer: A client is a computer or software application that requests services or resources from a server.
A web browser is an example of a client.

items.followUp: What information is placed in the head section of an HTML document?

rubric.why: Identifies the HTML section being defined.
rubric.description: Names the body section or body tags.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the section.

rubric.why: Describes the contents of the body section.
rubric.description: States that it contains the content displayed on the web page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its contents.

modelAnswer: The body section is the part of an HTML document enclosed by the <body> and </body> tags.
It contains the content displayed in the browser window, such as text, images and lists.

items.followUp: Write the output of an HTML ordered list containing two items, A and B.

rubric.why: Recognizes that the ul element displays an unordered, bulleted list.
rubric.description: Shows the items as a bulleted list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct list style.

rubric.why: Includes both list entries in the output.
rubric.description: Shows the word item twice as separate entries.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of writing an algorithm before programming a solution?

rubric.why: Shows that planning begins with understanding what must be solved.
rubric.description: Identifies understanding or analysing the problem as part of planning.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the problem is understood or analysed.

rubric.why: Explains that a solution is organised into ordered actions.
rubric.description: States that the solution is broken into steps arranged in order.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning ordered steps.

rubric.why: Names a way to represent the planned solution.
rubric.description: Mentions an algorithm, flowchart, or other suitable representation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a suitable representation.

rubric.why: Shows how planning helps check or improve a solution before coding.
rubric.description: States that the plan can be checked or tested to find errors or ensure correctness.

modelAnswer: Planning a solution means deciding in advance how a problem will be solved.
First, understand and analyse the problem, including its inputs and desired outputs.
Break the solution into clear, ordered steps and represent them with an algorithm or flowchart.
Check the plan for correctness and errors before writing the program.

items.followUp: Name and briefly explain three common problem-solving strategies.

rubric.why: Identifies a strategy that simplifies a complex problem by splitting it into manageable parts.
rubric.description: Names and explains divide and conquer or decomposition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the strategy and 1 mark for a correct explanation.

rubric.why: Identifies reasoning backward from the desired result toward the starting point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct strategy and explanation.

rubric.why: Identifies testing possible solutions and learning from the results.
rubric.description: Names or explains trial and error.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct strategy and explanation.

modelAnswer: Divide and conquer: Break a large problem into smaller, manageable problems and solve them one at a time.
Working backwards: Start with the desired result and reason backwards to determine the steps needed.
Trial and error: Try possible solutions, check their results, and improve the solution until it works.
